N1.title: The general oracle problem was known decades ago.
N1.evidence_after: Confirmed. Weyuker 1982; Barr et al. TSE 2015. Q1=NO.
N1.residual: LOW as a novelty claim; HIGH if the paper were sold as introducing oracles.
N1.defense: Cite the oracle problem as background. Claim only the DSP reference-adequacy audit.

N2.title: Sphere separability by LP is textbook convex optimization.
N2.evidence_after: Confirmed. Astorino–Gaudioso; Tax–Duin SVDD; Boyd–Vandenberghe. Q2=NO.
N2.residual: LOW if named as a diagnostic; FATAL if named as a new theorem.
N2.defense: Call Γ^amb an unrestricted-center adequacy diagnostic, not a new separator.

N3.title: The finite-set geometry is mathematically elementary.
N3.evidence_after: Coefficient ambient: separable=19 non-separable=1; Type A/B/C/D = 1/19/0/0; exact-rational=3.
N3.residual: MEDIUM. Elementary does not mean the DSP measurement was already done.
N3.defense: Sell the hierarchy + certificates on S_t, not the expansion of ||i-c||^2.
N3.more_science: NO unless certificates are only NUMERICAL_LP_ONLY.

N4.title: The paper merely applies software-testing ideas to filters.
N4.evidence_after: No matching DSP paper found that runs this three-level audit on independently labeled masks.
N4.residual: MEDIUM. A reviewer can still call it 'testing applied to DSP'.
N4.defense: The scientific object is mask-feasible sets vs realization balls — a filter-evaluation result.
N4.more_science: Optional later: one more specification family. Not required to finish Phase 3A.

N5.title: The result depends on one magnitude-mask task family.
N5.evidence_after: Still 20 magnitude-mask tasks. Phase 3A did not add families.
N5.defense: State the universe explicitly. Do not claim all DSP correctness.
N5.more_science: A second family would help a journal version; not Phase 3A.

N6.title: The unrestricted center is not itself a realizable DSP implementation.
N6.evidence_after: Asymmetry is explicit: no ambient center ⇒ no realizable reference rescues a single-center Euclidean oracle; an ambient center ≠ a realizable filter.
N6.residual: LOW if Type A; HIGH if Type B is sold as 'a better filter exists'.
N6.defense: Keep the asymmetry in any future sentence. Never infer realizability from a center.

kstar_rationale: Type B is the dominant coefficient outcome: an unrestricted Euclidean center (often a halfspace / center at infinity) recovers the frozen labels, but no observed valid realization does. The remaining reference-oracle question is exactly catalog complexity K* over observed valids. Phase 3A does not run K*.
blocker_why: unrestricted centers restore coefficient separability for a large majority of tasks
Q3: The manuscript-specific object is a certified three-level adequacy audit of realization-reference scoring against specification-defined FIR/IIR mask membership on a frozen independently labeled finite universe — not the oracle problem and not sphere LP.
Q4: NO — a testing reviewer can correctly say the oracle problem and sphere LP are known, but cannot correctly say that this frozen DSP universe was already shown to be non-spherically-separable under the paper's confirmatory embedding with certificates.
Q5: PARTIAL — ambient rescue would re-open 'a better geometric center exists' and weaken the claim that specification predicates are needed to represent validity.

A.name: conservative
A.text: Specification–reference mismatch, continuous correctness audit, and empirical geometry on the frozen corpus.
A.resistance: 6.0 — still open to 'bad reference' until Level 3 is mentioned.

B.name: geometry diagnostic
B.text: Fixed reference → best observed valid reference → unrestricted ambient center, with distinct symbols G_r, G_obs^*, Γ^amb.

C.name: reference-oracle adequacy audit
C.text: Combine specification membership, continuous certification, fixed-center gap, observed-center robustness, and unrestricted-center separability certificates.
C.page_cost: medium-high on 4 pages; one paragraph + pointer to supplement if needed.
C.resistance: 8.5 if certificates are exact or high-precision.

contribution.why: The three-level hierarchy is the new scientific object and fits a 4-page budget.
